value.rationale: Balanced sign alternation is the canonical highest-frequency zero-drift input for an adaptive optimizer. The result shows a qualitatively stronger effect than denominator oscillation alone: Yogi can rectify that balanced input into systematic linear parameter motion because the two gradient parities receive different effective learning rates. It also identifies exact mechanisms that suppress the effect—arithmetic locking and the source's own gradient-square initialization—so the statement directly clarifies the role of initialization and additive second-moment phase in the method's central effective-learning-rate mechanism.
